title: Jira vs Plane
comparison_markdown:
# Jira vs Plane

## Overview

Jira is the industry-standard issue and project tracking tool from Atlassian used for agile software development. Plane is a modern open-source alternative with a clean, fast interface.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Jira charges $7.75-$14.50/user/month; Plane is free to self-host
- **Complexity**: Jira is notoriously complex and slow; Plane is designed to be fast
- **Customization**: Jira has extensive workflow customization; Plane is simpler but improving
- **Integrations**: Jira integrates with the entire Atlassian ecosystem; Plane offers REST API access
- **Performance**: Plane modern architecture delivers significantly faster page loads

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Jira | Plane |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $7.75-$14.50/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$388/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$1,550/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Jira

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Plane

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [makeplane/plane](https://github.com/makeplane/plane) * ~31k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Jira if:** Jira suits large enterprises invested in the Atlassian ecosystem or teams needing highly customized workflow automation.

**Choose Plane if:** Plane is ideal for startups and small-to-mid teams tired of Jira complexity.

## Migration Path

Export Jira issues as CSV, then import into Plane using the CSV importer. Custom fields and automations will need to be recreated.

## Our Take

Plane is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Jira tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Plane instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Jira, switching to self-hosted Plane will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Jira until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Jira paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Plane free to use?
Yes. Plane is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Jira to Plane?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Jira data, follow the Plane import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Plane get regular updates?
Yes. Plane has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Plane without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Plane development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced July 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Jira](https://atlassian.com/jira) and [Plane](https://plane.so) before making decisions.*
meta_description: Plane is a free, self-hosted alternative to Jira. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.

title: Trello vs WeKan
comparison_markdown:
# Trello vs WeKan (2026)

## Overview
Trello and WeKan are project management tools that help teams organize and track their work. This comparison is useful for teams considering switching from Trello to WeKan, particularly those who value data ownership and self-hosting. The core use case for both tools is task and project management, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Trello offers a free plan with limited features, while WeKan is free and open-source, with no costs associated with usage.
* Data ownership: WeKan allows teams to self-host their data, giving them full ownership and control, while Trello stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: Trello is generally easier to set up and use, with a more intuitive interface, while WeKan requires more technical expertise to self-host.
* Scalability: Trello is designed to handle large teams and projects, with features like enterprise-level security and support, while WeKan's scalability depends on the team's self-hosting capabilities.
* Integration with Google Drive: Trello has a native integration with Google Drive, while WeKan relies on third-party integrations.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Trello | WeKan |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $5+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $250/month (standard plan) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1000/month (standard plan) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
### Trello
* Easy to use and set up
* Integrates with many third-party tools
* Scalable and secure
* Offers a free plan with limited features
* Limited control over data ownership
### WeKan
* Free and open-source
* Self-hosting available for full data control
* Customizable and extensible
* Community-driven development
* Limited support and documentation

## When to Choose Each
Trello is a good choice for teams who value ease of use and don't mind storing their data on proprietary servers. It's suitable for large teams and projects, with features like enterprise-level security and support. WeKan, on the other hand, is ideal for teams who prioritize data ownership and control, and are willing to invest time and resources into self-hosting and customizing the tool. It's suitable for small to medium-sized teams who value flexibility and customizability.

## Migration Path
1. Export Trello boards in JSON format using the Trello API or a third-party tool.
2. Set up a WeKan instance on a self-hosted server.
3. Use the WeKan import tool to import the exported Trello data.
4. Configure WeKan to match the team's workflow and needs.
5. Test and verify the migration to ensure all data is intact and functional.

## Our Take
WeKan is not yet production-ready for most users, as it requires technical expertise to self-host and customize. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that WeKan's scalability depends on the team's self-hosting capabilities, which can be a challenge for large teams. However, for teams who value data ownership and control, and are willing to invest time and resources, WeKan is a viable alternative to Trello.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) who don't need enterprise-level support
* Teams who prioritize data ownership and control
* Teams with technical expertise to self-host and customize WeKan
* Teams who don't need native integration with Google Drive
* Teams with simple project management needs

## FAQ
### Can I self-host WeKan on my own server?
Yes, WeKan is designed to be self-hosted, and teams can install it on their own servers for full data control.
### Is WeKan free?
Yes, WeKan is free and open-source, with no costs associated with usage.
### Can I migrate my Trello data to WeKan?
Yes, Trello data can be exported in JSON format and imported into WeKan using the WeKan import tool.
### Does WeKan have a mobile app?
Not yet, WeKan is primarily a web-based application, but mobile support is planned for future development.
### Is WeKan suitable for large teams?
WeKan's scalability depends on the team's self-hosting capabilities, so it may not be suitable for very large teams without significant technical expertise.

# Google Workspace vs Nextcloud (2026)

## Overview
Google Workspace and Nextcloud are two popular productivity and collaboration platforms that cater to the needs of individuals, teams, and organizations. This comparison is beneficial for users who are looking for a cost-effective and feature-rich alternative to traditional productivity suites, with a key reason to switch being the desire for greater control over data ownership and costs. The core use case for both tools is to provide a suite of productivity applications, including email, calendar, document editing, and file storage.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Google Workspace has a per-user monthly fee, while Nextcloud is free and open-source, with costs limited to server maintenance and infrastructure.
* Data Ownership: Nextcloud allows users to host their data on their own servers, giving them full control over their data, while Google Workspace stores data on Google's servers.
* Setup Complexity: Google Workspace is generally easier to set up, with a more streamlined onboarding process, while Nextcloud requires more technical expertise to self-host.
* Scalability: Google Workspace is highly scalable, with automatic upgrades and maintenance, while Nextcloud's scalability depends on the user's server infrastructure.
* Integration: Google Workspace has native integration with Google Drive, while Nextcloud has integration with a wide range of third-party apps through its marketplace.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Google Workspace | Nextcloud |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $6-$18/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $300-$900/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,200-$3,600/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Google Workspace:**
* Easy to set up and use
* Highly scalable and reliable
* Native integration with Google Drive
* Wide range of third-party apps available
* Robust security features
**Nextcloud:**
* Free and open-source
* Self-hosting option for full data control
* High degree of customizability
* Integration with a wide range of third-party apps
* Limited support for certain file types

## When to Choose Each
Google Workspace is ideal for teams and organizations that require a streamlined and easy-to-use productivity suite, with a focus on collaboration and integration with other Google apps. It is well-suited for small to medium-sized businesses, as well as enterprises that require a high degree of scalability and reliability. Nextcloud, on the other hand, is perfect for individuals and teams that value data ownership and control, and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and maintaining their own server infrastructure. It is ideal for users who require a high degree of customizability and are comfortable with self-hosting.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from Google Workspace using the Google Takeout service, which allows you to download your data in a variety of formats, including CSV and JSON.
2. Set up your Nextcloud server and configure the necessary apps and integrations.
3. Use the Nextcloud Importer tool to import your data from Google Takeout, which supports a range of formats, including CSV and JSON.
4. Configure your Nextcloud instance to meet your specific needs, including setting up user accounts, groups, and permissions.
5. Test your Nextcloud instance to ensure that all data and apps are functioning as expected.

## Our Take
Nextcloud is a production-ready alternative to Google Workspace for many users, offering a high degree of customizability and control over data ownership. However, it is worth noting that Nextcloud's self-hosting option can be complex and require significant technical expertise, which may be a limitation for some users. For users who value data ownership and control, and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up and maintaining their own server infrastructure, Nextcloud is an excellent choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) that require a cost-effective and customizable productivity suite
* Individuals who value data ownership and control, and are comfortable with self-hosting
* Medium-sized businesses (10-50 users) that require a high degree of customizability and integration with third-party apps
* Large enterprises (more than 50 users) that require a high degree of scalability and reliability, and are willing to invest in server infrastructure
* Users who do not require native integration with Google Drive, and are looking for a more open and customizable alternative

## FAQ
### Can I use Nextcloud with my existing Google account?
No, Nextcloud requires a separate account and authentication system. However, you can use Nextcloud's Google Drive integration to access your Google Drive files from within Nextcloud.
### Is Nextcloud compatible with all file types?
Not yet, Nextcloud has limited support for certain file types, such as Microsoft Office files. However, it does support a wide range of open formats, including ODF and PDF.
### Can I migrate my Google Workspace data to Nextcloud automatically?
Yes, Nextcloud provides an importer tool that allows you to import data from Google Takeout, which supports a range of formats, including CSV and JSON.
### Is Nextcloud secure?
Yes, Nextcloud has a strong focus on security, with features such as encryption, two-factor authentication, and access controls.
### Can I use Nextcloud on my mobile device?
Yes, Nextcloud has mobile apps for Android and iOS, which allow you to access your files and data on the go.
